articles.title: India's First Indigenous Bullet Train Takes Shape At BEML's Bengaluru Facility, Designed To ...
articles.content: Nov 05, 2026 | Updated 12:38 PM GMT+5:30 Save & read from anywhere! Bookmark stories for easy access on any device or the Swarajya app . India's first indigenously manufactured bullet train is under development at BEML's Bengaluru facility for the Mumbai–Ahmedabad High-Speed Rail corridor, with a planned operational speed of 249 kmph and a maximum test speed of 280 kmph. The National High Speed Rail Corporation Limited (NHSRCL), in a statement issued on 1 November, detailed the train's technical specifications, passenger amenities and safety features, outlining how the eight-coach trainset is being developed to meet Indian operating conditions. The train will measure approximately 202 metres in length and accommodate around 557 passengers, including two designated spaces for persons with reduced mobility. Its eight-coach configuration will comprise four motor cars and four trailer cars, with seven standard-class coaches featuring 3×2 seating and one executive-class coach offering 2×2 seating. The design also allows two eight-coach trainsets to be coupled into a 16-coach formation for future operations, providing the flexibility to increase passenger capacity as demand grows. Passenger facilities will include ergonomically designed seats with adequate legroom, LED lighting, wide windows, overhead baggage racks and additional floor-mounted luggage stands for larger bags. Power outlets for laptops and mobile devices, modern bio-digester toilets and sealed gangways connecting the coaches will also be provided. The train will feature a multilingual passenger information system, with LCD screens and automated announcements delivering journey-related information in English, Hindi and regional languages. Emergency communication units will allow passengers to contact train crew, while a Wi-Fi-based infotainment system will provide access to preloaded entertainment and information content. Accessibility has been incorporated into the train's design through level boarding, retractable footsteps to minimise gaps between train doors and platforms, wheelchair-accessible doors, designated seating and toilets, and Braille-enabled signage. Each coach will be equipped with two heating, ventilation and air-conditioning units to maintain suitable interior temperature and humidity levels under different climatic conditions. Sound insulation in the carbody and floor structure, noise-damping coatings, bogie covers and aerodynamic fairings are intended to reduce noise and improve passenger comfort. On the technical side, the train will operate on a 25 kV, 50 Hz single-phase alternating-current traction system. Regenerative braking technology will enable energy recovery during deceleration, contributing to improved operational efficiency. Its aerodynamic nose and carbody profile have been optimised using computational fluid dynamics simulations to reduce air resistance, turbulence and tunnel pressure waves. The sealed carbody is also designed to limit pressure variations experienced by passengers, particularly during high-speed tunnel operations. Driving cabs at both ends will incorporate an intelligent onboard control system to support operational decision-making and communication with the control centre. The indigenous trainset is being developed as part of India's broader efforts to establish domestic high-speed rail manufacturing capabilities. articles.title: 45 Mins To 15 Mins! India's 1st Public Ropeway Project In Varanasi To Cut Travel Time On ...
articles.content: Home / India / Trending / 45 Mins To 15 Mins! India’s 1st Public Ropeway Project In Varanasi To Cut Travel Time On THIS Stretch The Varanasi public transport ropeway is estimated to cost ₹675 crore and will cover approximately 4.2 km. The project is planned with around 220 cable cars. by Ashmeet Guliani Updated: November 05, 2026 10:30 AM Share Cover Image Courtesy: @avimuktkashii_/Instagram Varanasi is an ancient city with tight, winding lanes and heavy street traffic. People often get stuck in traffic, which is why India is set to launch its first public transport ropeway project. It could take you from Varanasi Cantt Railway Station to Godowlia Chowk in just 15 minutes. Note that this journey used to take around 45 minutes by road! Here’s what you need to know. Varanasi Ropeway Project To Launch Soon View this post on Instagram A post shared by Mehul Malviya | Avimukt Kashii (@avimuktkashii_) According to The Economic Times, Varanasi is all set to introduce India’s first public transport ropeway, which will connect Varanasi Cantt Railway Station to Godowlia Chowk. With narrow lanes in the city, the journey can take around 45 minutes by road. But this new project is quicker and is expected to cover the same stretch in just 15-16 minutes. And yes, this ropeway project is going to benefit both locals and tourists alike, as Varanasi, also known as Kashi, sees a huge influx of tourists every day. The ropeway is nearing its launch later this year, but a content creator, Mehul Malviya (@avimuktkashii_), recently shared a glimpse of his experience on Instagram. He took his followers on a virtual journey on this ropeway in Varanasi. The video showed the cable car, which looks clean and has space for multiple passengers. The design of the cabins is also inspired by the Kashi Vishwanath Temple and Varanasi’s holy ghats. Also Read: Dev Deepawali In Varanasi: 7 Experiences That Make The Trip Worth It! Ropeway Station Featured Modern Facilities In the video, we can see that Mehul took a smooth ride over the city’s busiest stretch. The views from the sky looked amazing, and we could also see residential areas from above. In another post, the creator also shared glimpses of the Varanasi Ropeway station, which features elevators and several other modern facilities. According to The Economic Times, the Varanasi public transport ropeway is estimated to cost ₹675 crore and will cover approximately 4.2 km. The project is planned with around 220 cable cars, each of which can carry up to 10 passengers. articles.title: Anti-ragging mobile app launched in Keralam - The New Indian Express
articles.content: THIRUVANANTHAPURAM: With the aim to strengthen student safety, the government on Wednesday launched a mobile app that allows students to anonymously report ragging and other campus-related grievances. It has been named after JS Siddharth, who died allegedly by suicide in 2024 following ragging at College of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Wayanad. The government also launched a project to establish 300 science centres across the state to promote scientific temper and inquiry-based learning among young people. The launch of the Student Aspiration Survey, aimed at paving the way for major reforms in higher education, and the inauguration of a special online course on scientific temper, prepared in collaboration with C-DIT, were also held. Chief Minister V D Satheesan inaugurated the first sub-centre of Jawaharlal Nehru Centre for Scientific Temper project at Government Women’s College, Thiruvananthapuram. He also launched the Siddharth Student Welfare mobile app. In his inaugural address, Satheesan stressed the need to revive the scientific spirit and rational thinking envisioned by India’s first PM, Jawaharlal Nehru, both on campuses and in society. He also warned that the government would adopt a zero-tolerance approach towards ragging and ensure those responsible were brought to justice. Presiding over, Higher Education Minister Roji M John said the government was actively considering a Siddharth Anti-Ragging Act to provide stronger legal framework for tackling the menace. He also said the project envisaged setting up 300 sub-centres under the leadership of the Kerala State Higher Education Council, to foster scientific temper and humanism among nearly 15 lakh young people. At a time when fake news and superstition spread rapidly in the digital space, the centres would help students distinguish facts from myths, he said. Prof Achuthsankar S Nair, vice-chairman of Higher Education Council; B Ashok, Principal Secretary, higher education, and other dignitaries attended.
